messages:
pagerbot: INCIDENT ALERT: high pending queue in gpu-pool-usw2-3 (capacity_exhausted). severity=sev2. triggered at 2026-03-15T14:41:08Z. paging alice_oncall and oncall-sre.

alice_oncall: seeing it — queue length 1200, 95% of requests hitting throttle. dropping tail latency > 4s. digging in now.

ben_sre: grabbing metrics. cloud-autoscaler reports failed scale attempts due to 'no valid placement' (fragmentation). logs: 
```
autoscaler: attempted_scale=8 -> failed_reasons=[MIG_SIZE_MISMATCH, BINPACK_FAIL]
pod_bindings_pending=482
```

carla_mlinfra: this looks like the MIG/shape mismatch we warned about. a bunch of recent model-rollouts requested 1xA100/80GB equivalent but cluster only has mixed MIG slices (1/2/3-way). autoscaler won't stitch slices.

dave_serving: confirmed — new v2-generation jobs request large contiguous GPU, but pool is heavily fragmented with many 1/4 slices. scheduler can't fit, so capacity is effectively stranded.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) throttle non-SLA tenants (low priority) 2) emergency rebalance to consolidate slices to larger MIG sizes 3) admit temporary CPU fallbacks for embedding jobs. which is fastest?

emma_support: several customers already reporting timeouts — cs case #5432 (image-gen startuplabs) and #5437 (search embeddings). customers impacted: two on hosted API with soft-SLOs.

ben_sre: throttling config: we can flip host-throttle -> throttled for label tenant:free-tier via console, takes ~30s. rebalance is heavier (needs node drains + instance replacement) ~20-30m.

carla_mlinfra: can we patch autoscaler to allow cross-pool packing as emergency? risk: higher latency from remote pools. but might let big jobs land. quick patch would be a flag flip.

alice_oncall: do it. carla, enable cross-pool packing and increase max_scale by +10 while we rebalance. ben, prep throttle command. dave, start a plan for targeted MIG consolidation on a small set of nodes (usw2-3 zone).

infra-bot: Runbook step executed: set throttle policy 'free-tier' -> ON by alice_oncall.

ben_sre: throttle applied. observed immediate drop in incoming requests from free-tier. queue down from 1200 -> 740 in 90s. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

carla_mlinfra: cross-pool packing flag turned on. autoscaler logs now show some placements to pool-usw2-1 (cold zone) but with 80-120ms added network tail. inbound queue now 420.

dave_serving: starting targeted MIG consolidation. plan: pick 6 nodes with many 1/4 slices, cordon+drain, replace with 1/1 large MIG instances. rolling operation script below:
```
# simplified
for node in $CANDIDATES; do
  kubectl cordon $node
  kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  gcloud compute instances delete $node --zone usw2-3 --quiet
  gcloud compute instances create $node --machine-type a2-highgpu-1g --gpu-mig-slice 1 --zone usw2-3
done
```

ben_sre: note — evac logs show some pods failing to gracefully shutdown during drain (model checkpoint saver stuck). we should set pod gracefulTimeout=45s for these batches.

alice_oncall: adjust gracefulTimeout where needed, move noncritical batch jobs to CPU fallback. carla, watch for regression alerts.

carla_mlinfra: bumping gracefulTimeout and excluding long-running batch jobs from initial drain. requeueing heavy checkpoints to warm nodes.

emma_support: messaging to customers: posting on status page that we see degraded throughput and that teams are throttled to protect latency for paid customers. drafting note, will post once we confirm sustained improvement.

ben_sre: midway update: 3/6 nodes replaced. MIG consolidation freed ~4 large-GPU slots. queue down to 190. pending pods 32. autoscaler scale events now succeed for large requests.

dave_serving: observed a weird binpack failure on one node: kernel OOM during pod eviction, investigating. might be transient.

alice_oncall: if OOM recurs, rollback that node and re-create with slightly larger instance type. avoid rolling more until stable.

carla_mlinfra: cross-pool packing produced expected latency hit; customers with soft-SLOs noticed but core paid tenants stable. still seeing a few stranded 1/4 slices but less impactful.

infra-bot: Deploybot: canary of autoscaler patch completed at commit sha abc123.

ben_sre: final numbers: queue peak 1200 -> now 18. throttle in place for free-tier, 6 nodes consolidated, autoscaler max increased temporarily +10 then returned. no data loss, customer errors mostly timeouts.

alice_oncall: transitioning to recovery mode. summary for handoff:
- root cause: mixed MIG sizing + recent spike of large contiguous GPU requests => scheduler binpack failures -> stranded capacity -> autoscaler failure to find placements (scale aborted).
- mitigations applied: free-tier throttle, cross-pool packing flag, emergency MIG consolidation (6 nodes), autoscaler max increase, temporary CPU fallback for noncritical jobs.
- impact: hosted free-tier degraded, 2 soft-SLO customers had timeouts, paid tenants remained within SLO after mitigations.
- open items: investigate why autoscaler refused placement rather than pro-actively triggering rebalance; add proactive periodic defragmentation job; improve rollout checklist for v2 model that requests large contiguous GPUs.

carla_mlinfra: leaving triage note in infra repo, will schedule follow-up postmortem. assigning owners: autoscaler root-cause: carla_mlinfra, scheduler improvements: dave_serving, customer comms + RCA: emma_support.

alice_oncall: handing off to ben_sre for overnight watch. cross-pool flag will be rolled back in 2hr if stable. notify if queue > 150 or pending pods > 50.

ben_sre: taking oncall. will keep watching. good recovery; big props to everyone. :raised_hands:

emma_support: status page update posted. customers acknowledged.

pagerbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (degraded -> stable) at 2026-03-15T15:05:15Z. duration ~24m.

alice_oncall: creating postmortem stub now. will include timeline, metrics, and follow-ups.

carla_mlinfra: adding recommended fixes: automated defrag, enforce MIG-request validation on model rollout, and autoscaler fallback to burst-cold-pools earlier.

ben_sre: leaving final note — consider a 'stranding' telemetry alert (pending pods + high free-slice ratio) so we catch earlier.

alice_oncall: thanks all. handoff complete.
